meta.inputs_absent_note: These were named as inputs for this stage but do not exist on disk: they were produced by no stage that wrote to the repository. The structural check and link probe in this directory (structural.json, link-probe.json) stand in for the automated part; no reviewer output exists for any entry beyond the 12 in review-pass1/2.json.

rules.R1-R8: non-OR entries: APPROVED only if two verifiers agree on identity (same edition, both identified), rights tier (A1 or A2, same class) and extraction path (intersecting adapters, both say verbatim use); APPROVED-LINKOUT-ONLY if both say link-out only and agree on identity and tier; any REJECT-vs-other, any request for human review or any disagreement is NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW with both rationales kept; both REJECT is REJECTED
rules.R9-R13: OR entries: APPROVED-CROSSWALK iff report number, author, side and first page agree with the OCR header index of the Internet Archive scan; APPROVED-POINTER for Part XIII pages iff the page exists and its side label agrees; otherwise NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW
rules.R14: DUPLICATE only on a hard identity (same HathiTrust volume id confirmed by the catalog API, or same document id)
rules.R16: NOT-VERIFIED: nothing is approved on automated checks alone

description_issues: The linked page is a third-party transcription, not the SHSP scan; it differs from the printed text in a few places ('withing', 'Devine', 'until' for 'till', 'endeavored', a doubled 'many of the'), and its <title> is empty.

issues_pass1: The linked page is a third-party transcription, not the SHSP scan; it differs from the printed text in a few places ('withing', 'Devine', 'until' for 'till', 'endeavored', a doubled 'many of the'), and its <title> is empty.
The article is entitled 'A Soldier's Account of the Gettysburg Campaign' in the body but is listed as 'Gettysburg Campaign - A Soldier's Letter' in the volume contents: same item.

The entry title says '9th Virginia Cavalry', which the letter itself does not state outright; it is established from the Hanover paragraph and from entry 596 (father's regiment) and the House Divided blog.
IA metadata 'date' for the SHSP volume is 1876 (the series start), not 1883: use the volume's own contents/running heads for dating.
Written to his mother in the field in heavy rain, so it is a contemporaneous but unpolished and somewhat hearsay-laden account (e.g. losses and the Hagerstown fight reported second-hand).
issues_pass2: The listed URL is a volunteer transcription (Gettysburg Discussion Group, unchanged since 2010) with about 20 word-level deviations from the 1883 print: omitted words, 'withing', 'Devine', 'up' for 'us', 'be' for 'he', 'in' for 'at', and a doubled 'many of the'. It fails a verbatim check and must not be the quote source. The first pass said 'a few places'.

The link is http only: https on gdg.org fails with a revoked certificate (CRYPT_E_REVOKED), so tools that upgrade http to https cannot fetch it. Single-host hobby site with an empty <title>, so there is some link-rot risk; prefer the Internet Archive scan.

The entry carries no year or page range. Add 'written 13 July 1863; SHSP 11 (1883): 320-327'. The IA 'date' metadata for vol. 11 says 1876 (series start), not 1883, so date from the title page and page headers instead.

Title naming: the body is 'A Soldier's Account of the Gettysburg Campaign. Letter from George W. Beale (son of General R. L. T. Beale)', while the volume contents list 'Gettysburg Campaign - A Soldier's Letter, by George W. Beale'. These are the same item.

The 9th Virginia Cavalry attribution is not stated in the letter. It is established independently by R. L. T. Beale's 1899 regimental roster (George W. Beale, 1st Lt., Co. C), SHSP vol. 11 ('his four sons' in the Ninth Virginia Cavalry), and the letter's own 9th/13th Virginia references.

The letter is contemporaneous (13 July 1863, ten days after East Cavalry Field) but is a hurried, tired, partly second-hand account, written in rain during the retreat. It exaggerates the Rockville capture (about 200 wagons and 12,000 mules, against Stuart's 125 wagons), reports the Hagerstown and Fortieth Virginia losses by hearsay, and gives no calendar dates (the one date, 'June - -', is blank). Treat as perspective, not fact. The 1883 print also cannot be compared with the 1863 manuscript, so editorial changes by SHSP cannot be ruled out.

Small internal ambiguity: 'Colonel Payne, Captain Billingsly of this regiment ... were captured'. Stuart's report gives Payne as Lieut. Col., 4th Virginia Cavalry (temporarily commanding the 2nd NC). Do not attribute Payne to the 9th Virginia.
